title: High-speed train collision near Toledo kills 68 in Spain
dek: A Renfe high-speed train ran into the back of a stationary Iryo train near Urda on 28 October. Authorities put the death toll at 68; the cause is under investigation.
happened: At about 8:53 a.m. on 28 October, a Renfe AVE train travelling from Madrid to Seville struck the rear of an Iryo train that had stopped on the same line near Urda, in Toledo province. The two trains were carrying 544 people. Authorities put the death toll at 68, and 58 people needed medical treatment.

sides.says: Transport Minister Óscar Puente said a computer fault in the main signalling system had stopped all trains on that stretch, and that an "inexplicable" order from a control centre then let the Renfe train continue. Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez declared three days of mourning and said any negligence would be addressed with "utmost firmness".

Spanish media citing Transport Ministry sources reported a possible error by an operator at the control centre in Madrid; El País reported that the train passed a stop signal. The cause has not been confirmed. A court in Orgaz is investigating.

next: Investigators are working to establish whether the signalling fault, the control-centre order or both caused the collision. It is the second deadly crash this year involving trains of the same two companies, after a collision in southern Spain in January killed 46 people.
summary: Spain is in mourning after a state-run Renfe high-speed train hit the back of a privately run Iryo train near Urda, in Toledo province, on the morning of 28 October. Both were travelling from Madrid towards Seville. Authorities put the death toll at 68, which WION reports makes it Spain's deadliest rail accident in a decade. The transport minister described a signalling fault that had halted traffic, followed by an order that let the Renfe train move on; other reports point to a possible operator error or a passed stop signal. None of these has been confirmed, and the prime minister has said any negligence will be pursued.
